title: Height and residue transcendence degree for a one-variable polynomial algebra
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and put $P=R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. A domain means a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $Q\subset P$ and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be prime ideals with $Q\cap R=\mathfrak p$ under the constant-polynomial inclusion. For a prime $\mathfrak a$ of a ring $A$, put $\kappa(\mathfrak a)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak a)$ and let $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak a)$ be the supremum of the lengths of strict prime chains ending at $\mathfrak a$. With the residue-field inclusion induced by $R\hookrightarrow P$ and transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree], one has $\operatorname{trdeg}_R P=1$ and
$$\operatorname{ht}(Q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(Q)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+1.$$

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), proof, Case I: polynomial algebra, flat height decomposition and the two polynomial-fibre prime cases.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-transcendence-degree] with one variable, $\operatorname{trdeg}_R P=1$. The monomials $1,T,T^2,\ldots$ form an $R$-basis by uniqueness of coefficients, so [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] makes $R\to P$ flat. The algebra $P$ is generated by $T$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. A product of nonzero polynomials has nonzero leading coefficient, so $P$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), proof, Case I: polynomial algebra and its two fibre-prime cases.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $C=P\otimes_R k$. Identify $C$ with $k[T]$ by $f\otimes a\mapsto a\overline f$, whose inverse sends $\sum a_iT^i$ to $\sum T^i\otimes a_i$. The tensor balancing relation verifies the maps are inverse ring maps and preserve $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], $Q$ corresponds to a prime $q$ of $C$, with inverse image $Q$ under $j:P\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-residue-field-iso], $\kappa(Q)\cong\kappa(q)$ over $k$: on scalars the map sends the residue of $r/s$ to the same fraction, since $s\notin\mathfrak p$. For a prime $\mathfrak a$ of a ring $A$, the residue field $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak a)$ of the statement is identified with $A_{\mathfrak a}/\mathfrak aA_{\mathfrak a}$ of these nodes by $\bar a/\bar s\mapsto$ the class of $a/s$ ($s\notin\mathfrak a$): this is well defined and injective because $a/s\in\mathfrak aA_{\mathfrak a}$ exactly when $a\in\mathfrak a$, surjective because every $a/s$ is hit, and compatible with ring maps; we use it for $\mathfrak p$, $Q$ and $q$. Thus the relative transcendence degrees agree.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), proof, Case I: polynomial algebra and its two fibre-prime cases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fiber-prime-height] to the flat map $R\to P$ and the fibre prime $q$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1 and the contraction hypothesis. Switch the tensor factors by $f\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes f$ to match its convention. Prime chains are carried bijectively by this ring isomorphism. Its heights are dimensions of prime localizations, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] identifies each of them with the supremum of lengths of prime chains ending at the prime, the height of the statement. So its conclusion is $\operatorname{ht}(Q)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{ht}(q)$.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), proof, Case I: polynomial algebra and its two fibre-prime cases.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-dimension-one], $\dim k[T]=1$. If $q=(0)$, the only prime below it is itself, so $\operatorname{ht}(q)=0$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] applied to the finite type domain $k[T]$ gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(q)=1$. If $q\ne(0)$, the chain $(0)\subsetneq q$ and the dimension bound give $\operatorname{ht}(q)=1$. Every prime containing $q$ equals $q$, since a strict enlargement would give a chain of length two. Inverse image under the quotient map bijects primes of $k[T]/q$ with primes of $k[T]$ containing $q$; its inverse sends a prime $r$ containing $q$ to $r/q$. Thus the only prime of this nonzero domain is zero, and its dimension is zero. It is generated over $k$ by the class of $T$. The same dimension/transcendence-degree node, now applied to $k[T]/q$, gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(q)=0$.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), proof, Case I: polynomial algebra and its two fibre-prime cases.

proof.text: In either case $\operatorname{ht}(q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(q)=1$. Substitute Step 2 into Step 3 and add the residue transcendence degree to obtain $\operatorname{ht}(Q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(Q)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+1$. Together with Step 1 this proves both assertions.
